Description: The official or common name of the road from the OpenStreetMap data (e.g., "US Route 9W" or "Main Street").
The name of the road from which the current road segment originates.
The name of the road to which the current road segment connects.
The name of the road as recorded by the field surveyor.
General comments about the overall crossing from the surveyor.
Text notes from the surveyor describing the location of the crossing.
The name of the stream as recorded by the field surveyor.
The official name of the stream or river from the National Hydrography Dataset, if available.
The distance in meters between the original NAACC survey point and its final matched location on the road network.
A score from 0 to 100 indicating the confidence in the match. Higher scores represent more confident matches based on distance, name similarity, and match type.
The unique, persistent identifier for the crossing from the NAACC database.
The type of crossing structure recorded by the surveyor (e.g., 'Bridge', 'Culvert', 'Multiple Culvert').
The shape and material of the structure's inlet (e.g., 'Round Culvert', 'Box Culvert').
The shape and material of the structure's outlet.
Specific comments about the physical structure(s) from the surveyor.
The unique identifier for the NHDPlus flowline that the crossing is on.
A numeric code representing the general category of the hydrographic feature (e.g., 460 for Stream/River).
A human-readable description of the waterway type (e.g., 'StreamRiver', 'CanalDitch').
A more detailed description of the stream, indicating if it is perennial (flows year-round), intermittent, or ephemeral.
The estimated mean annual flow of water in the stream, measured in cubic feet per second. This provides a measure of the waterway's size and power.
The raw internal score calculated for the match (lower is better). Used to determine the `match_confidence_score`.
The normalized version of the OSM road name used for similarity comparison.
The normalized version of the NAACC road name used for similarity comparison.
The raw similarity score (0-100) between the OSM and NAACC road names.
The strategy used for the match: 'road_flowline_intersection_match' (preferred) or 'shortest_line_to_road_span' (fallback).
Numeric road classification based on the OpenLR standard, where lower numbers indicate higher-order roads.
The highway type string corresponding to the primary road class.
A boolean flag indicating if the OSM way is a standard roadway (not a service road, trail, etc.).
A boolean flag indicating if the OSM way is a service road.
A boolean flag indicating if the NAACC crossing is on a trail.
A boolean flag indicating if the NAACC road is unnamed.
A boolean flag indicating if the NAACC crossing is on a driveway.
A boolean flag indicating if there is a significant inconsistency between the OSM and NAACC road types (e.g., a roadway matched to a trail).
A brief text description of the logic used to select the final match (e.g., "High confidence decision" or "Min match rank").
Internal identifier for the starting node of the road segment in the OpenStreetMap network graph.
Internal identifier for the ending node of the road segment in the OpenStreetMap network graph.
Internal identifier for parallel edges between the same two nodes in the OpenStreetMap network graph.
Indicates if the matched road segment was classified as a 'BRIDGE' or 'NONBRIDGE' span.
The index of the road span within a larger road segment.
The index of the intersection within a road span, for cases where one span has multiple intersections.
